text:
sasha: heads up — noticed weird telemetry in console: tenant 'acme' dashboard shows a huge request spike at 09:12 but our request traces point to 'phoenix' traffic. not sure if metrics attribution or UI is mixing tenants.

dana: yikes. is this only telemetry or user-facing data? any PII risk? :eyes:

sasha: UI shows only counts, no PII. but quota dashboard for acme also got charged. could be costing customers.

mike: can you paste a minimal repro or the headers from the trace?

sasha: here's the simplest curl we used to trace the bad row — note the header we set and the response id returned by internal-api: ```curl -H 'X-Tenant-ID: phoenix' -H 'Authorization: Bearer token' https://internal-api.redwood/v1/insights -d '{"q":"/panels/42"}' -i``` response: `202 Accepted` with envelope id `env_0x9ab`

sasha: then async-telemetry logs for env_0x9ab show processed-> tenant="" (empty). two entries: `enqueue env_0x9ab tenant=phoenix` then later `process env_0x9ab tenant=`.
lucy: that smells like the batching aggregator dropping X-Tenant-ID when compressing envelopes. we changed that code last month to reduce envelope size.
mike: where does the envelope get serialized? internal-api -> event-queue -> telemetry-worker -> timeseries-store. suspect serialization in event-queue (batcher.go).
dana: could be header normalization middleware we added for cookie-less requests. it rewrites headers to lower-case and we added a whitelist — maybe X-Tenant-ID got filtered.
sasha: grep shows middleware whitelists: [authorization, content-type, user-agent, request-id]. x-tenant-id is not present. but earlier traces show it existed at internal-api before enqueue.
infra-bot: deploy-notice: rollout internal-api v1.14 started at 2023-11-01T09:05:12Z to canary in us-west2.
mike: that matches timeframe. the change to header whitelist was in v1.14.
lucy: quick mitigation: add X-Tenant-ID to the whitelist in batcher and force re-enqueue of pending unprocessed envelopes? risky.
dana: can we patch batcher to include tenant in envelope body (not header) as a fallback, then roll forward? safer to preserve identity across queueing.
sasha: agree. patch plan: (1) add tenant field into envelope payload in event-queue (backfill on receive), (2) update telemetry-worker to prefer payload. this avoids depending on header whitelist.
mike: i'll open a PR and tag @lucy for review. we should also run a quick query to find other envelope types missing tenant and estimate affected customers (billing impact).
lucy: will instrument a search over queue logs for `process tenant=` and export a list.
dana: action items: mike PR (hotfix) -> review -> canary deploy -> run backfill -> update billing team. anyone want to own notifying support/CS?
sasha: i'll ping CS with short note and hold until we have a mitigation.
infra-bot: rollback window: 30m for internal-api canary.
mike: PR opened: https://git.redwood/p/telemetry/+/789 — includes unit test for envelope tenant copy. applying to canary now.
lucy: found ~1200 processed envelopes with empty tenant between 09:06-09:20 in us-west2. likely a handful of tenant dashboards affected. exporting list to #support-private.
dana: good. once canary looks stable, plan a patch release. also we should add an integration test that ensures tenant propagation through the event queue.
sasha: agreed. note for follow-up: audit the other headers we whitelist so we don't repeat this for any identifier (x-org, x-workspace).
mike: will add integration tests and a checklist item to the rollout docs. thanks team :thumbsup:
